classification_reasons: Spec tight: every open question (refuse redirects, refuse datetime, direct tzdata marker) closed with a decision in spec/plan; acceptance measurable by four named regression tests plus the owner's Windows check.

Blast radius moderate, not small: the HTTP opener is rebuilt by hand (every download path), parse_date callers (make_request, clear_cache) change behaviour, and pyproject.toml gains a platform-marked dependency and a packaging table; no risk-list hit.
This round's delta (commit f62fcfd) is three trailing '# noqa: DTZ001' comments plus a reflow of one parametrize list in tests/test_data.py, with no runtime effect.
attempted: Intent: the owner's review (fix-requests.json, CHANGES_REQUESTED) asked for '# noqa: DTZ001' on the three deliberate naive datetimes, parametrize values on separate lines, nothing else; tests/test_data.py:540, 563, 565 carry exactly that, and the parametrize list at 537-543 is split one value per line. The edit matches fix-response.md's planned edit verbatim. The change as a whole still answers intent items 1-3.

Spec and plan: the diff (diff-deploy.patch) touches only the files plan.md lists (tests/test_data.py, app/data/http.py, app/data/params.py, pyproject.toml, .gitignore) plus change-folder artifacts; the four Proof tests are present.
Line length: line 563 measures exactly 100 characters, line 565 98, line 540 well under; within ruff line-length = 100.

Proof: test.log (89 passed, names test_data.py) and lint.log ('All checks passed!') are from 18:27Z, before f62fcfd; the round only adds comments, so pytest results cannot change. The lint verdict that matters is CI's pinned ruff 0.16.9, which flagged DTZ001; the noqa targets exactly those codes. The local-ruff RUF100 skew the caller mentions is outside the requested change and CI is the authority; not a reason.

Tests weakened? Tests were unlocked by the owner (status.yaml tests_unlocked_by: luissiviero) for this request only; the delta changes no assertion, parameter value or test body; both naive and aware datetime cases still run; no pre-existing test touched (all test_data.py hunks are additions after line 498 plus imports).

Could tests pass with bug present: test_datetime_bound_is_refused_not_a_type_error and test_clear_cache_refuses_a_datetime_bound still require InvalidRequestError matching 'not a datetime' (a TypeError would fail them); clear_cache test seeds a day file so the comparison path is reached.
Blast radius: no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml, policies/**) in the diff; .github/workflows/ci.yml untouched; risk-list hits none, so no brief written.
Skip markers: none added in the diff.
Policies: no per-file-ignores workaround added, no secrets, no network in tests; the suppression is scoped per line with the specific code, as the owner asked.
Claims against today's code: http.py opener handler list and params.py parse_date datetime guard in the diff match plan.md steps 2-3; pyproject marker and [tool.setuptools] match step 4.
Drive: commands.drive not relevant to this round; no proof/ files in the delta.
